question: How does Circle CCTP V2 move native USDC to or from Stellar, and which fee claims must be checked live?

golden.answer: Circle added Stellar mainnet CCTP support on 2026-05-18, and SDF and Circle announced it live on 2026-05-19; Stellar is CCTP domain 27. CCTP burns native USDC on the source chain and mints native USDC on the destination, with no wrapped token. Inbound transfers set both mintRecipient and destinationCaller to the CctpForwarder contract, which forwards to the G, M or C recipient named in hook data. Stellar USDC's seventh decimal stays on Stellar because CCTP messages use 6. Fees are live values: as of 2026-11-14 Circle's fee API showed Fast/Standard 0/0 for 27→0 and 1 bp/0 for 0→27.
keyFacts: Stellar mainnet CCTP support came on 2026-05-18 and was announced live on 2026-05-19.
CCTP burns native USDC on the source chain and mints native USDC on the destination.
Inbound transfers set mintRecipient and destinationCaller to the CctpForwarder contract.
CCTP messages use 6 decimals, so Stellar USDC's seventh decimal stays on Stellar.
Fees are dated live values from Circle's fee API, not fixed.
avoid: Do NOT say CCTP locks USDC and issues a wrapped Stellar token.
Do NOT present CCTP fees as permanent or the transfer as exactly 1:1 after all costs.
golden.notes: Accept either milestone date when it is labeled (technical support 2026-05-18, public announcement 2026-05-19). Fee figures are dated observations; accept a later dated figure from Circle's fee API.

corroboration.claim: Use Circle's CctpForwarder for Stellar G-, M-, or C-address recipients; incorrect mintRecipient or destinationCaller values can strand funds.
Stellar USDC has 7 decimals while CCTP messages use 6; the seventh outbound decimal remains on Stellar.

Circle documents per-route Fast/Standard CCTP fees and the /v2/burn/USDC/fees endpoint to query them; the specific 2026-07-11 readings (0/0 for 27→0, 1 bp/0 for 0→27) are a dated probe observation recorded in the golden, and callers must re-query.
Circle transfer fees are separate from network resource, relayer, integrator, and swap charges.
CCTP locks USDC and issues a wrapped Stellar token.
Every CCTP route is permanently fee-free and exactly 1:1 after all costs.
Circle added Stellar mainnet CCTP support on 2026-05-18.
